claims.verbatim:
HOSPITAL SHIP FALCON, May 30, 1866.
Dr. SWINBURNE—I have to report the arrival of the
steamship Union, Captain Palmer, from Liverpool May 12,
at this station. She sailed with four hundred and thirty-
four passengers, and on her arrival here many of them
were down with cholera. The first case occurred on the
18th, in the person of a native of Denmark, who died
twelve hours after the attack. Thirty-three died on the
passage, mostly of cholera, She had thirty-four sick on
her arrival here. They were transferred to this ship,
many in a dying condition.

HOSPITAL SHIP FALCON, May 30, 1866.
Dr. SWINBURNE—I have to report the arrival of the
steamship Union, Captain Palmer, from Liverpool May 12,
at this station. She sailed with four hundred and thirty-
four passengers, and on her arrival here many of them
were down with cholera. The first case occurred on the
18th, in the person of a native of Denmark, who died
twelve hours after the attack. Thirty-three died on the
passage, mostly of cholera, She had thirty-four sick on
her arrival here. They were transferred to this ship,
many in a dying condition.

An unofficial report says that the steamship
Union, from Liverpool, sixteen and a half
days out, arrived at quarantine at New York
yesterday evening with four hundred and
thirty-four passengers, thirty-three of whom
died of cholera on the passage. Fifteen cases
of cholera still remain on board.
